assumedContext: No primary filing retrievable; findings rest on H1 2026 and FY2025 results releases and trade press.

findings.claim: The renewables number in the thesis is a pipeline, not an asset base, and the ratio is the finding. The global operational portfolio is 1.2 GW, generating roughly 0.9 TWh in H1 2026, against a total pipeline exceeding 12 GW. Ten parts of every eleven are not built.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: And it is not intended to become one. Metlen runs an explicit asset-rotation model: build, then sell. It completed the sale of a 283 MW UK solar portfolio in H1 2026 and targets 1.0-1.5 GW of annual delivery. The pipeline is inventory, not installed base.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: That distinction is the single most important reframing in this dossier. A 12 GW pipeline owned by an independent power producer is a future annuity to be discounted. A 12 GW pipeline owned by a developer on an asset-rotation model is a stream of development margins and construction contracts, which are cyclical, execution-dependent, and worth a materially lower multiple.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from the disclosed business model

findings.claim: The pipeline composition is disclosed and is weighted to the two technologies with the lowest barriers to entry: roughly 57% photovoltaic and 35% storage. Neither has a component bottleneck of the kind Siemens Energy enjoys in transformers; solar modules and battery cells are in global oversupply.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: The genuinely scarce asset in the group is the metals complex. Aluminium of Greece is a fully integrated bauxite-alumina-aluminium operation, the largest in the European Union, and the EU is not permitting new primary smelters. That is a Constellation-type barrier: it cannot be rebuilt.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from the EU primary aluminium landscape

findings.claim: The expansion at that asset is specific and dated: 2m tonnes of bauxite, 1.26m tonnes of alumina and 50 tonnes of gallium a year, EUR 295.5m committed, bauxite from 2026, alumina and gallium phasing from 2027, full scale 2028.
findings.label: MANAGEMENT GUIDANCE

findings.claim: Greek hydrology is an underappreciated swing factor. Hydroelectric generation more than doubled in H1 2026 on higher rainfall, and Greek renewable generation rose 21% year on year. Part of the record half is weather, and weather does not compound.
findings.label: FACT

risks.text: The 12 GW pipeline is development inventory in oversupplied technologies, not an installed base. Only 1.2 GW is operational, and the model is to sell what is built.
Development and EPC margins are cyclical and execution-dependent, and deserve a materially lower multiple than contracted generation.
Part of the record H1 was hydrology. Hydroelectric generation more than doubled on rainfall, which does not compound.
The gallium and alumina expansion is not yet producing. Full-scale operation is a 2028 event with normal commissioning risk.

Further asset rotation disposals at disclosed margins

conclusions: The pipeline figure in the thesis is real and understated — it now exceeds 12 GW — but only 1.2 GW is operational. Ten parts in eleven are not built.

And they are not meant to be held. Metlen runs an explicit asset-rotation model targeting 1.0-1.5 GW of annual delivery, and sold a 283 MW UK solar portfolio in H1. The pipeline is inventory, not installed base.

That reframing is the most important in this dossier. A pipeline owned by a developer is a stream of development margins and construction contracts — cyclical, execution-dependent, and worth a lower multiple than contracted generation.
The composition compounds it: roughly 57% PV and 35% storage, the two technologies with no component bottleneck and global oversupply. This is the opposite of Siemens Energy's transformer position.

The group's genuinely irreplaceable asset is the one the thesis mentions least — Aluminium of Greece, the EU's largest integrated bauxite-alumina-aluminium operation, in a bloc that is not permitting new primary smelters.
thesisImpact: Phase 2 inverts the thesis's emphasis. The renewables pipeline it leads with is the group's weakest-barrier business, and the metals complex it treats as the junior partner is the only asset here that cannot be rebuilt. Phase 5's sum-of-the-parts must apply a development multiple to renewables and an infrastructure multiple to metals, not the reverse.
